review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the formal-frontier repo for uses of the simp-related declarations. The file has only two simp lemmas, `prefixIdeal_zero` and `prefixIdeal_succ`. Both are `rfl` equations that unfold the `Nat.rec` definition one step at a time on `0` and `k+1`. They are oriented from the opaque recursor to its explicit unfolding, so I see no cycle, no competing rule and no unwanted expansion. The only expansion at literal `d + 1` is intended. `prefixIdeal_zero` has no overlapping simp lemma, because `prefixIdeal` is a local definition. The other equivalences (`isRightUnimodular_iff_span_range_eq_top` and `Submodule.right_span_range_eq_top_iff_ideal_span_range_eq_top`) are bridge lemmas. Marking them `simp` would risk competing with the existing `isRightUnimodular_iff_right_span_eq_top` in `RowKernel`, and no use in the repo needs it. The proofs use plain `simp`/`simpa` on ad hoc goals, and nothing there points to a missing canonical simp lemma. I could not run Lean, so I did not test any simp behaviour.
